▶ CHAPTER 0 6 · DATA FLOW VARIABLES · FACTS · REGISTERS 8 MIN ▸ WHAT — T hree sour c es of d a t a Variables parameterize desired state. F acts are auto-gathered system data. R egisters capture task output for later use. DATA FLOWS DOWNHILL TO MODULES Inventory → group/host v ars → play/task v ars → facts + r egisters → module / t emplat e Variables: author-defined values ( app_port: 8080 ) from inventory, group_vars/ , host_vars/ , play, task, or --extra- vars . Facts: discovered values ( ansible_os_family , ansible_default_ipv4.address ) collected by ansible.builtin.setup at play start (gather_facts). Registers: per-host results of a prior task ( register: host_out ), used by later tasks, conditionals, or templates. ▸ WHY — O ne pl a y b ook , m a ny hosts Same playbook must behave differently per host: web-01 listens on 8080 with one certificate, web-02 on 8081 with another. Hard-coding values per host duplicates playbooks. Data flow explains *how* values travel from inventory and discovery into modules, templates, and conditionals. ▸ WHERE DOES IT FIT — Da t a l a ne Inventory vars → group_vars → host_vars → play vars → task vars → facts/registers → module/template/conditional

▶ CHAPTER 0 6 · DATA FLOW ( CONT . ) VARIABLES · FACTS · REGISTERS 8 MIN ▸ HOW IT WORKS — P re c eden c e , f ac ts , registers Precedence exists because specificity must win: general defaults lose to host-specific values. Simplified order (low → high): role defaults → group_vars/all → group_vars/web → host_vars/web-01 → play vars → task vars → extra- vars Collision example: group_vars/all.yml sets app_port: 8080 , host_vars/web-01.yml sets app_port: 9090 → web-01 renders 9090, others render 8080. ansible-playbook -e app_port=9999 overrides everything (operator intent wins for one run). Facts: gather_facts: true (default) runs setup first, populating ansible_facts . Disable with gather_facts: false for speed when facts are unused. R egisters: register stores stdout , stderr , rc , changed per host — never shared across hosts unless hostvars is read explicitly. ASPECT VARIABLE FACT REGISTER Author You write it Ansible discovers it A task captures it Example app_port: 8080 ansible_facts.os_family host_out.stdout Refresh File-defined rank Re-gathered every run Re-registered every run Override --extra-vars wins Cannot override, only use Read via hostvars cross-host E ngineering · V ol

▶ CHAPTER 0 6 · DATA FLOW ( CONT . ) VARIABLES · FACTS · REGISTERS 8 MIN ▸ PRACTICAL — Ob serve d a t a flow - name: Show data flow hosts: web vars: app_port: 8080 tasks: - name: Show variable ansible.builtin.debug: msg: "port {{ app_port }}" - name: Capture hostname ansible.builtin.command: cat /etc/hostname register: host_out changed_when: false - name: Show captured output ansible.builtin.debug: var: host_out.stdout - name: Show discovered fact ansible.builtin.debug: msg: "family {{ ansible_facts.os_family }}" COMMAND ──────────────────────── ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini data.yml -e app_port=9999 Meaning: run play with CLI override. Expected: msg: "port 9999" on all hosts — proves extra-vars beats file vars. R emove - e → web-01 shows 9090 (host_vars), others 8080. Why it matters: proves precedence is deterministic, not magic. Common failure: quoting msg="port {{ app_port }}" with double quotes inside Y AML double quotes → use single outer or block scalar. E ngineering · V ol 2 5 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 6 · DATA FLOW ( CONT . ) VARIABLES · FACTS · REGISTERS 8 MIN ▸ WHAT CAN FAIL SYMPTOM LIKELY CAUSE PREVENTION AnsibleUndefinedVariable: 'app_port' is undefined Typo or vars file in wrong directory group_vars/ must sit beside inventory file; verify with ansible-inventory --graph --vars Precedence surprise (wrong port) Higher-specificity file wins silently debug: var=app_port per host before template task host_out.stdout empty Task skipped/failed before register Check host_out.rc , host_out.skipped ; guard with when: host_out.rc is defined Facts missing gather_facts: false set globally Re-enable per play or call ansible.builtin.setup explicitly [ GOTCHA ] Precedence is not inheritance depth — it is specificity + source rank. Group of one host still loses to that host's host_vars. Always verify with --list-hosts + debug before templating. ▸ REAL - WORLD CONNECTION Team stores defaults in group_vars/all.yml (port, TLS paths), per-environment overrides in group_vars/prod.yml , per- host exceptions in host_vars/ . Promotion from staging to prod changes inventory path, not playbook. changed counts stay clean because data varies, not tasks. E ngineering · V ol 2 6 ok c h a nged

▶ CHAPTER 0 6 · DATA FLOW ( CONT . ) VARIABLES · FACTS · REGISTERS 8 MIN ▸ LAB — Ob serve / E xe c ute / V erify Objective: prove precedence + facts + registers. Prereqs: group_vars/all.yml ( app_port: 8080 ), host_vars/web- 01.yml ( app_port: 9090 ). 1. ansible-inventory -i inventory.ini --graph --vars → Observe merged vars per host 2. ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini data.yml --check → Execute dry run, watch msg per host 3. Verify web-01 shows 9090, others 8080. Explain: host specificity wins. 4. Re-run with -e app_port=9999 → Verify all show 9999. Explain: operator override is highest rank. Failure drill: rename host_vars/ to hostvars/ → re-run → undefined/wrong value → fix directory name. ▸ I nterview c he c k Interview Where do variables come fr om, and which wins? Inventory, group/host vars files, play/task vars, facts, registers, extra-vars. More specific beats more general; extra-vars beats files. Facts are discovered, registers are captured per host from prior task results. [ NEXT ] Data varies per host. Next: branch and repeat with that data — conditionals, loops, filters. E ngineering · V ol 2 7 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 7 · LOGIC CONDITIONALS · LOOPS · FILTERS 7 MIN ▸ WHAT — B r a n c h , repe a t , tr a nsform Conditionals ( when ) branch tasks. Loops ( loop ) repeat one task over many items. Filters transform data inside Jinja2 expressions ( {{ value | filter }} ). - name: Install nginx only on web ansible.builtin.package: name: nginx state: present when: inventory_hostname in groups['web'] - name: Ensure users exist ansible.builtin.user: name: "{{ item }}" state: present loop: [alice, bob] Jinja2 filters: {{ app_port | default(8080) }} , {{ groups['web'] | length }} , {{ app_name | upper }} . ▸ WHY — F leets diverge Real fleets are not uniform: web needs nginx, db needs postgres; ten users, not one. Without logic the author copies tasks per host — drift follows. when keeps one task with a guard; loop keeps one task with many items; filters keep expressions safe when data is missing. ▸ WHERE DOES IT FIT — L ogi c c onsumes d a t a Variables/facts/registers (Ch 06) → when/loop/filter (this chapter) → template/handler (Ch 08) Conditionals read facts and registers ( ansible_facts.os_family == "Debian" , host_out.rc == 0 ). Loops feed {{ item }} into modules. Filters guard undefined data

▶ CHAPTER 0 7 · LOGIC ( CONT . ) CONDITIONALS · LOOPS · FILTERS 7 MIN ▸ HOW IT WORKS — E v a lu a tion per host when is a Jinja2 expression evaluated per host, without {{ }} delimiters. loop executes the task once per item, with item and ansible_loop metadata. Filters pipe left value through right function; they chain ( {{ name | lower | trim }} ). Combined example: - name: Deploy app config per host ansible.builtin.template: src: app.conf.j2 dest: /etc/app/app.conf loop: "{{ app_instances }}" when: app_enabled | default(true) Loop over app_instances (from group vars), skipped entirely when app_enabled is false. loop_control: label keeps output readable for long lists. BRANCH PER HOST AT RUN TIME WHEN TRUE Task runs on this host → module converges → result recorded WHEN FALSE Task SKIPPED on this host → play continues → no change, no failure E ngineering · V ol 2 9 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 7 · LOGIC ( CONT . ) CONDITIONALS · LOOPS · FILTERS 7 MIN ▸ FILTER FIELD GUIDE — T he dozen th a t ca rry you Filters group by job. Learn these twelve and you can read any playbook: JOB FILTERS EXAMPLE Missing-safe default , is defined {{ app_port | default(8080) }} Branch in one line ternary {{ tls_enabled | ternary('https', 'http') }} Types int , bool , string , list {{ replicas | int + 1 }} Lists length , join , map , select , unique , sort {{ groups['web'] | length }} , {{ users | map(attribute='name') | join(',') }} Dicts dict2items , combine {% for kv in app_env | dict2items %} with kv.key / kv.value Text upper , lower , trim , replace {{ app_name | lower | trim }} Data formats to_json , from_yaml , to_nice_yaml {{ cfg | to_nice_yaml }} for debug output The safety pattern first: when: myvar is defined and myvar == "x" never explodes on missing hosts; {{ myvar | default('x') }} never aborts a template. Write every optional value one of these two ways. E ngineering · V ol 2 1 0 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 7 · LOGIC ( CONT . ) CONDITIONALS · LOOPS · FILTERS 7 MIN ▸ LOOP VARIANTS — B eyond fl a t lists Dictionaries need dict2items (a dict cannot loop directly): - name: Export environment entries ansible.builtin.lineinfile: path: /etc/app/env line: "{{ item.key }}={{ item.value }}" loop: "{{ app_env | dict2items }}" Long or slow loops stay readable and controllable: - name: Pull service images ansible.builtin.command: docker pull {{ item }} loop: "{{ images }}" loop_control: label: "{{ item }}" pause: 2 Polling waits for reality instead of sleeping blindly: - name: Wait for healthy endpoint ansible.builtin.uri: url: "http://{{ inventory_hostname }}:8080/health" register: health until: health.status == 200 retries: 30 delay: 10 until re-runs the task until the condition holds (or retries run out); combine with changed_when: false for pure checks so successful polls report OK , not CHANGED . E ngineering · V ol 2 1 1 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 7 · LOGIC ( CONT . ) CONDITIONALS · LOOPS · FILTERS 7 MIN ▸ PRACTICAL — R un b r a n c h + repe a t COMMAND ──────────────────────── ansible web -i inventory.ini -m ansible.builtin.debug -a "msg={{ ansible_facts.os_family }}" Meaning: show discovered family per host. Expected: Debian / RedHat per target — proves facts exist before when uses them. - name: Guarded install hosts: all tasks: - name: Install nginx on Debian web only ansible.builtin.package: name: nginx state: present when: - inventory_hostname in groups['web'] - ansible_facts.os_family == "Debian" Why it matters: two-condition guard prevents installing on wrong OS family. Common failure: when: "{{ condition }}" with delimiters → always truthy string; write bare when: condition . E ngineering · V ol 2 1 2 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 7 · LOGIC ( CONT . ) CONDITIONALS · LOOPS · FILTERS 7 MIN ▸ WHAT CAN FAIL SYMPTOM LIKELY CAUSE PREVENTION template error while templating string Undefined var or bad filter chain {{ var | default('x') }} , test with debug first Task skipped unexpectedly when evaluated false on that host --check -vv shows skip reason per host when with {{ }} always runs Non-empty string is truthy Bare expression: when: rc == 0 Loop output unreadable (100 items) Default item echo loop_control: { label: "{{ item.name }}" } [ GOTCHA ] when does not use {{ }}. when: ansible_facts.os_family == "Debian" converges. when: "{{ ... }}" is a non- empty string — always true. ▸ REAL - WORLD CONNECTION Patch window: same playbook against staging then prod. when: env == "prod" gates the disruptive restart; loop over critical_services restarts each; | default guards hosts missing the optional maintenance_window var. --limit web plus --check --diff previews exactly which hosts branch where. ▸ LAB — Ob serve / E xe c ute / V erify Objective: prove branch + repeat. Prereqs: inventory with web and db groups. 1. ansible all -i inventory.ini -m ansible.builtin.setup -a "filter=ansible_os_family" → Observe fac

▶ CHAPTER 0 8 · FILES TEMPLATES AND HANDLERS 7 MIN ▸ WHAT — R ender files , defer rest a rts ansible.builtin.template renders a Jinja2 file ( src: *.j2 ) to the managed node. Handlers run once at end of play — only if notified by a task that reported CHANGED . RENDER , COMPARE , NOTIFY ONCE TEMPL ATE → COMPARE → CHANGED → notif y → HANDLER ONCE Five notifying tasks still restart the service exactly once, at play end. - name: Render nginx config ansible.builtin.template: src: nginx.conf.j2 dest: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf mode: '0644' notify: Restart nginx handlers: - name: Restart nginx ansible.builtin.service: name: nginx state: restarted Template ( nginx.conf.j2 ): server { listen {{ app_port | default(8080) }}; server_name {{ inventory_hostname }}; } ▸ WHY — C onfig v a ries , rest a rts a re expensive Config files differ per host (port, TLS path, server name) — copy ships identical bytes, template ships per-host rendering. Restarting a service per task is noisy and can flap: five config tasks → five restarts. Handlers batch: five tasks notify, handler runs once at end, only if something actually changed. E ngineering · V ol 2 1 4 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 8 · FILES ( CONT . ) TEMPLATES AND HANDLERS 7 MIN ▸ WHERE DOES IT FIT — Da t a + logi c → files + ac tions Variables/facts (Ch 06) + when/loop (Ch 07) → template renders → compare → CHANGED → notify queue → handler once copy = static bytes. template = bytes computed from data. lineinfile / blockinfile = surgical edits (prefer full template when the file is owned; prefer line edits for foreign files like /etc/sudoers.d/ fragments). ▸ HOW IT WORKS — C omp a re , queue , flush Template renders locally, compares checksum with remote dest, transfers only on difference → CHANGED or OK . notify appends handler name to per-play queue; duplicates collapse to one entry. At play end (or meta: flush_handlers mid- play), each queued handler runs once in handler order, not notify order. listen: groups multiple notify names onto one handler. handlers: - name: Restart web stack listen: Restart nginx ansible.builtin.service: name: nginx state: restarted validate: guards syntax before install ( validate: "nginx -t -c %s" ); failed validation → task FAILED , dest untouched. E ngineering · V ol 2 1 5 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 8 · FILES ( CONT . ) TEMPLATES AND HANDLERS 7 MIN ▸ PRACTICAL — Ob serve notify - on - c h a nge COMMAND ──────────────────────── ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini site.yml First run: TASK [Render nginx config] changed: [web-01] → RUNNING HANDLER [Restart nginx] changed: [web- 01] . Second run: both ok — handler silent. Proof of deferred idempotent restart. Why it matters: handler silence on second run is the convergence signal for config management. Common failure: handler name typo → ERROR! The requested handler 'Restart ngnix' was not found — names match exactly unless listen aliases. ▸ WHAT CAN FAIL SYMPTOM LIKELY CAUSE PREVENTION could not find src: nginx.conf.j2 Wrong src path (role vs playbook relative) src relative to templates/ in role, or playbook dir; verify with --check -vv Handler never runs Task reports OK (already converged) or name mismatch Change a var to force CHANGED ; use listen: for aliases Handler runs every time Template renders nondeterministically (timestamp inside) Remove volatile content from template; use validate + --diff to inspect Bad config deployed No validate validate: "nginx -t -c %s" on template task [ GOTCHA ] "OK" on template means

▶ CHAPTER 0 8 · FILES ( CONT . ) TEMPLATES AND HANDLERS 7 MIN ▸ LAB — Ob serve / E xe c ute / V erify Objective: prove render → notify → once. Prereqs: nginx.conf.j2 with {{ app_port }} . 1. Run play → Observe changed + handler run 2. Re-run → V erify ok , handler silent. Explain: no diff, no notify. 3. Change app_port in host_vars/web-01.yml → run → V erify only web-01 changes + handler runs for it. 4. Insert meta: flush_handlers between two config tasks → V erify handler runs mid-play. Failure drill: rename handler → run → not-found error → fix with listen: alias. ▸ I nterview c he c k Interview Why handler s instead of restarting in the task? Tasks may repeat; restarts must not. Handlers collapse many notifications into one run at play end, and only when a notifying task actually changed something — batching + convergence in one mechanism. [ NEXT ] Single play grows large with templates and handlers. Next: split into reusable units — roles and collections. E ngineering · V ol 2 1 7 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 9 · ORGANIZATION ROLES AND COLLECTIONS 8 MIN ▸ WHAT — R eus ab le units a nd their distri b ution Role = reusable unit with conventional directories (tasks, handlers, templates, defaults, vars). Collection = versioned distribution of roles plus modules and plugins, addressed by fully qualified names ( namespace.collection ). roles/web/ tasks/main.yml handlers/main.yml templates/nginx.conf.j2 defaults/main.yml vars/main.yml meta/main.yml Conventional layout: tunables in defaults (lose), assertions in vars (win). roles/web/ tasks/main.yml handlers/main.yml templates/nginx.conf.j2 defaults/main.yml vars/main.yml meta/main.yml - name: Configure web fleet hosts: web roles: - role: web vars: { app_port: 8080 } Install: ansible-galaxy collection install community.general . FQCN in tasks: community.general.ufw , ansible.builtin.template . ▸ WHY — P l a y b ooks do not s ca le fl a t One site.yml with 200 tasks is unreviewable: variables collide, handlers duplicate, copy-paste spreads. R oles give boundaries (defaults vs vars, tasks vs handlers); collections give versioning and sharing (pin requirements.yml , upgrade deliberately). Galaxy and private automation hub become the pa

▶ CHAPTER 0 9 · ORGANIZATION ( CONT . ) ROLES AND COLLECTIONS 8 MIN ▸ WHERE DOES IT FIT — O rg a niz a tion a fter me c h a ni c s Play → task → module (Ch 04) + data (Ch 06) + logic (Ch 07) + files (Ch 08) → role bundles them → collection ships them → ansible.cfg/CLI locates them defaults/main.yml = lowest precedence (safe to override). vars/main.yml = high precedence (role asserts). requirements.yml pins collections per project — same discipline as requirements.txt . ▸ HOW IT WORKS — R esolution a nd in c lusion Role search path: playbook roles/ dir → roles_path in ansible.cfg → Galaxy default. T ask inside role resolves templates/ and files/ relative to the role. import_role is static (parsed when playbook loads — when applies per task inside). include_role is dynamic (evaluated at execution — can loop over roles). - name: Static web role ansible.builtin.import_role: name: web - name: Dynamic per-env roles ansible.builtin.include_role: name: "{{ item }}" loop: [base, web] Collections: ansible-galaxy collection install -r requirements.yml ; reference namespace.collection.module . Short names ( template , package ) still resolve today but are obsolete — lint flags them, content us

▶ CHAPTER 0 9 · ORGANIZATION ( CONT . ) ROLES AND COLLECTIONS 8 MIN ▸ PRACTICAL — C onvert pl a y to role COMMAND ──────────────────────── ansible-galaxy role init roles/web ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini site.yml --check --diff Meaning: scaffold conventional layout, then dry-run role-based play. Expected: same changed/ok counts as flat play — proves refactor preserved behavior. Why it matters: refactor without behavior change is the organization proof. Common failure: couldn't resolve module/action 'my_module' → collection not installed or FQCN missing → ansible-galaxy collection install -r requirements.yml . ▸ WHAT CAN FAIL SYMPTOM LIKELY CAUSE PREVENTION couldn't resolve module/action Collection missing or short name FQCN + requirements.yml + ansible-galaxy install -r Role not found roles_path wrong or role beside wrong playbook ansible-config dump | grep -i roles_path ; keep roles/ beside site.yml import_* vs include_* surprise Static vs dynamic timing import for fixed structure; include for loops/conditionals on the include itself Vars collision across roles Same var name in two roles Namespace vars ( web_app_port ), defaults for overridables [ GOTCHA ] defaults/ loses to a

▶ CHAPTER 0 9 · ORGANIZATION ( CONT . ) ROLES AND COLLECTIONS 8 MIN ▸ LAB — Ob serve / E xe c ute / V erify Objective: extract tasks into role without behavior change. Prereqs: working flat site.yml from Ch 04. 1. ansible-galaxy role init roles/web → Observe scaffold 2. Move tasks/handlers/templates/vars into role dirs → point site.yml at roles: [web] 3. ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini site.yml --check --diff → Verify identical planned changes. Explain: organization, not behavior, changed. 4. Add requirements.yml with one collection → ansible-galaxy collection install -r requirements.yml → Verify FQCN task resolves. Failure drill: break roles_path in ansible.cfg → not-found error → ansible-config dump → fix path. ▸ I nterview c he c k Interview Role vs collection vs playbook? import vs include ? Playbook selects hosts and composes roles. R ole bundles tasks/handlers/templates/vars for one concern. Collection versions and ships roles+modules+plugins. import_* resolves at parse (static), include_* at run (dynamic, loopable). [ NEXT ] Organized automation is ready to be secured. Next: privilege boundaries and secrets — become and V ault. E ngineering · V ol 2 2 1 ok c h a nged f a i

▶ APPENDIX · CHEATSHEET CHEATSHEET — DATA TO ROLES FINALE A P re c eden c e ( low to high ) SOURCE WINS ? role defaults loses group_vars to host_vars host wins play to task vars task wins extra-vars -e always wins B L ogi c a nd F iles NEED USE Branch when: bare, no delimiters Repeat loop: + loop_control label Per-host file template + handler Share role to collection, FQCN ● OK — c onverged , no c h a nge ◐ CHANGED — c onverged , did c h a nge �� FAILED — did not c onverge E ngineering · V ol 2 2 2 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC
END ENGINEERING · VOL 2 VOL 3 — PRODUCTION ANSIBLE Vault, quality gates and CI/CD: from tested role to rolling fleet. E ngineering · V ol 2 2 3 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 1 0 · SECURITY VAULT · BECOME · SECRETS 8 MIN ▸ WHAT — L e a st privilege + en c rypted se c rets become escalates privilege (typically sudo) per play, role, or task. Ansible V ault encrypts variables and files so secrets live in Git safely and decrypt only at run time. SECRETS STAY ENCRYPTED UNTIL RUN TIME PLAINTEXT VAR → VAULT ENCR YPT → COMMIT SAFE → DECRYPT AT RUN - name: Configure web fleet hosts: web become: true become_user: root vars_files: - group_vars/prod/vault.yml tasks: - name: Deploy TLS key ansible.builtin.copy: src: tls.key dest: /etc/nginx/tls.key mode: '0600' ansible-vault encrypt group_vars/prod/vault.yml ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini site.yml --ask-vault-pass Vault file holds vault_tls_key , vault_db_password — referenced as {{ vault_db_password }} , never in plain vars. ▸ WHY — A utom a tion is a privileged se c ret - spre a der Playbooks run as root across fleets and touch credentials. Plain-text secrets in Git leak to every clone; blanket become: true with passwordless sudo everywhere widens blast radius. V ault + scoped become give two guarantees: secrets encrypted at rest in version control, privilege granted narrowly per task. P rodu c tion ·

▶ CHAPTER 1 0 · SECURITY ( CONT . ) VAULT · BECOME · SECRETS 8 MIN ▸ WHERE DOES IT FIT — S e c ure a fter org a nize Roles/collections (Ch 09) define vars → Vault encrypts the sensitive subset → become scopes who applies them → testing (Ch 11) verifies without leaking → CI/CD (Ch 12) injects vault password from CI secrets Do not confuse Ansible V ault (file/var encryption in-repo) with HashiCorp V ault (external secret store via lookup plugins). They compose: external vault supplies at run, Ansible V ault encrypts what must live in Git. ▸ HOW IT WORKS — E n c rypt , s c ope , inje c t Vault: ansible-vault encrypt|decrypt|view|edit|rekey per file; encrypt_string for inline values. Multiple vault IDs ( --vault-id prod@prompt ) separate environments. At run, password comes from prompt, file ( --vault-password-file ), or CI secret → file. no_log: true on secret-touching tasks suppresses output. Become: become: true + become_user + become_method: sudo (or su , runas on Windows). Scope narrowly: play default become: false , escalate only tasks needing root. --ask-become-pass for interactive sudo password; in CI use NOP ASSWD scoped sudoers or ephemeral privilege. - name: Read app status

▶ CHAPTER 1 0 · SECURITY ( CONT . ) VAULT · BECOME · SECRETS 8 MIN ▸ SUDO PITFALLS — P rivilege side : sudoers a nd b e c ome identity Most Ansible failures on Linux are not Ansible bugs — they are privilege, ownership, or interpreter mismatches. Learn the five usual suspects. 1. Sudoer s scope. Grant the automation user exactly what plays need, nothing more: ansible ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/systemctl *, /usr/bin/apt-get *, /usr/bin/yum * Blanket ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL works in labs and horrifies auditors; passworded sudo needs --ask-become-pass (interactive) or CI-managed credentials. Old RHEL/CentOS images also enforce Defaults requiretty — sudo over non- interactive SSH fails until that line is removed for the automation user. 2. Become identity . become_user decides *who you become*, default root . Database tasks often need the service account instead: - name: Vacuum app database community.postgresql.postgresql_query: query: VACUUM ANALYZE become: true become_user: postgres P rodu c tion · V ol 3 5 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 1 0 · SECURITY ( CONT . ) VAULT · BECOME · SECRETS 8 MIN ▸ SUDO PITFALLS — H ost side : ownership , SEL inux , interpreter 3. Owner ship and modes. Files created by a root-run task belong to root. Serve them to an app user and reads fail: - name: Deploy app config ansible.builtin.template: src: app.conf.j2 dest: /etc/app/app.conf owner: app group: app mode: '0640' Always set owner/group/mode on security-relevant files; verify with a second task using ansible.builtin.stat when the service is picky. 4. SELinux cont exts. On enforcing systems, correct mode with wrong context still denies: ansible web -i inventory.ini -m ansible.builtin.command -a "getenforce" # Enforcing? ansible web -i inventory.ini -m ansible.builtin.command -a "ls -Z /etc/app/" Fix with community.general.sefcontext + restorecon , or ansible.posix.selinux booleans ( httpd_can_network_connect is the classic) — never blanket setenforce 0 in production. 5. Python int erpreter. Modules execute in Python on the target. Minimal images lack it, or ship two versions: [web:vars] ansible_python_interpreter=/usr/bin/python3 Symptom MODULE FAILURE: /bin/sh: python: command not found → install python3 via a raw bootstr

▶ CHAPTER 1 0 · SECURITY ( CONT . ) VAULT · BECOME · SECRETS 8 MIN ▸ PRACTICAL — E n c rypt a nd run without le a king COMMAND ──────────────────────── ansible-vault encrypt_string 's3cr3t-db-pass' --name 'vault_db_password' Expected: vault_db_password: !vault | $ANSIBLE_VAULT;1.1;AES256... — paste into group_vars/prod/vault.yml , commit safely. COMMAND ──────────────────────── ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini site.yml --ask-vault-pass --check --diff Why it matters: proves encrypted vars decrypt at run and dry-run shows structure without exposing values (with no_log: true ). Common failure: Attempting to decrypt but no vault secrets found → password file path wrong or -- vault-id label mismatch. ansible-vault view group_vars/prod/vault.yml # read without decrypting to disk ansible-vault edit group_vars/prod/vault.yml # decrypt, edit, re-encrypt in one step ansible-vault rekey group_vars/prod/vault.yml # rotate the password on existing files view for inspection, edit for changes, rekey for rotation — the file stays encrypted at every step except inside the editor. P rodu c tion · V ol 3 7 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 1 0 · SECURITY ( CONT . ) VAULT · BECOME · SECRETS 8 MIN ▸ WHAT CAN FAIL SYMPTOM LIKELY CAUSE PREVENTION no vault secrets found Missing --ask-vault-pass / wrong password file CI secret → file → --vault-password-file ; test locally with prompt first Failed to escalate privilege sudoers denies or password needed Scoped NOP ASSWD for automation user; --ask-become- pass interactively Secret in logs Task echoes var without no_log no_log: true on secret tasks; audit with --check -vv in safe env Vault + HashiCorp V ault confused Same word, different tools Ansible V ault = encrypted files in repo; HCP V ault = lookup at run ( community.hashi_vault ) [ GOTCHA ] Encrypting a file does not fix over-broad privilege. V ault protects secrets at rest; become scoping protects hosts at run. Do both — one without the other leaves half the attack surface open. ▸ REAL - WORLD CONNECTION TLS key rotation: operator runs ansible-vault rekey per environment file, commits re-encrypted vault, opens PR showing only !vault blobs changed. CI holds vault password as protected secret, runs --check --diff for approval, then applies with serial: 1 . Audit trail = Git history of who changed which encrypte

▶ CHAPTER 1 0 · SECURITY ( CONT . ) VAULT · BECOME · SECRETS 8 MIN ▸ LAB — Ob serve / E xe c ute / V erify Objective: secret committed encrypted, applied with scoped privilege. Prereqs: group_vars/prod/vault.yml with one test secret. 1. ansible-vault encrypt group_vars/prod/vault.yml → Observe blob, git diff shows no plaintext 2. ansible-vault view group_vars/prod/vault.yml → Verify round-trip decrypt 3. Run play with --ask-vault-pass --check --diff → Verify task references {{ vault_db_password }} without printing it ( no_log: true ) 4. Set become: false at play, become: true only on privileged task → V erify least-privilege scoping. Failure drill: run without password → decrypt error → add --ask-vault-pass → converges. ▸ I nterview c he c k Interview How do secr ets reach hosts without living in plain t ext, and how is pr ivilege scoped? Secrets committed as V ault-encrypted vars/files, decrypted at run from prompt/file/CI secret with no_log guarding output. Privilege via become scoped per task ( become_user , least-privilege sudoers), not blanket root everywhere. [ NEXT ] Secure automation must be trustworthy before it is triggered automatically. Next: lint, test, and Molecule qu

▶ CHAPTER 1 1 · QUALITY LINT · CHECK · MOLECULE 7 MIN ▸ WHAT — T hree qu a lity g a tes ansible-lint enforces style, FQCN, and common mistakes statically. --check --diff dry-runs a playbook against real inventory without changing it. Molecule tests roles in ephemeral containers or VMs (create → converge → verify → destroy). THREE GATES BEFORE CI TRUSTS A ROLE LINT style + FQCN → CHECK + DIFF blast radius → MOLECULE converge twice → CI same gat es ansible-lint site.yml ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging site.yml --check --diff molecule test Molecule cycle: create (ephemeral host) → converge (apply role) → verify (assert state) → destroy . Second converge should report ok with zero changed — the idempotence proof. ▸ WHY — A utom a tion multiplies mist a kes A typo in one task runs on a hundred hosts in minutes. Lint catches the typo in seconds; check-mode previews blast radius; Molecule proves the role converges twice cleanly before CI ever touches staging. Without gates, every run is a fleet experiment. ▸ WHERE DOES IT FIT — Q u a lity b efore triggers Vault-secured roles (Ch 10) → lint (seconds) → check/diff (minutes, safe) → molecule (minutes, ephemeral) → CI/CD (Ch 12) runs

▶ CHAPTER 1 1 · QUALITY ( CONT . ) LINT · CHECK · MOLECULE 7 MIN ▸ HOW IT WORKS — S t a ti c , dry - run , ephemer a l Lint: rule-based ( yaml , fqcn , name[prefix] , no-changed-when ). Pin ansible-lint 6+ in dev requirements; ansible-lint --fix for safe auto-fixes. Check mode: modules report would-change without acting ( --check ); --diff shows file/service deltas. Command/shell tasks skip check unless check_mode: true is handled — another reason to prefer modules. Molecule: molecule init role acme.web -d docker ; molecule.yml defines platform, provisioner ( ansible_playbook ), verifier ( ansible asserts). verify.yml asserts converged state: - name: Verify hosts: all tasks: - name: Nginx is running ansible.builtin.assert: that: - "'nginx' in ansible_facts.services" ▸ PRACTICAL — Ga te a role lo ca lly COMMAND ──────────────────────── ansible-lint roles/web/ && ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging site.yml --check --diff Meaning: static rules, then dry-run delta. ▶ CHAPTER 1 2 · DELIVERY CI / CD — COMMIT TO FLEET 9 MIN ▸ WHAT — E very push drives a utom a tion s a fely CI/CD triggers ansible-playbook after Git push, with per-environment inventory. The pipeline runs the Ch 11 gates, previews with --check --diff , requires approval for prod, then converges the fleet and feeds results to observability. EVERY PUSH CAN REACH THE FLEET SAFELY GIT PUSH → LINT + TEST → STAGING DIFF → APPROVAL → PROD ROLLING Git push → CI (lint) → molecule → ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging --check --diff → approval → ansible-playbook -i inventories/prod → observability → feedback to Git Project structure: inventories/{staging,prod}/hosts.yml group_vars/{all,staging,prod}.yml host_vars/ roles/ site.yml ansible.cfg requirements.yml ▸ WHY — Ma nu a l runs do not survive s ca le SSH-loop runs depend on who runs them, from which laptop, with which vars. CI gives one runner, pinned versions, secret- injected vault passwords, and an audit trail per commit. S taging-then-prod with identical playbooks makes promotion a change of -i path, not a new procedure. P rodu c tion · V ol 3 1 4 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

Execution tuning ( strategy , forks , serial ) and inventory at scale (constructed inventory, group_vars layering) keep that convergence fast and scoped as fleets grow. ▸ HOW IT WORKS — S tr a tegies , s ca le , pipeline Execution strategies: linear (default, lockstep per task) vs free (hosts race ahead). forks: 20 caps parallelism; serial: 1 (or "25%" ) rolls hosts in batches for safe restarts. ansible-inventory --graph verifies selection before any run. - name: Rolling web update hosts: web serial: 1 tasks: - name: Render config ansible.builtin.template: src: nginx.conf.j2 dest: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf notify: Restart nginx handlers: - name: Restart nginx ansible.builtin.service: name: nginx state: restarted GitHub Actions sketch: checkout → setup Python → pip install ansible ansible-lint molecule → ansible-galaxy install -r requirements.yml → lint → molecule test → check/diff staging (artifa

Expected: graph shows web / db counts; --diff lists only intended lines. Any surprise line blocks promotion. Why it matters: the --diff artifact is what approvers review — not a prose description. Common failure: CI env lacks vault password → decrypt error → wire CI secret to --vault-password-file via temp file, never echo. ansible-playbook -i inventories/prod site.yml --check --diff # reviewed artifact ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging site.yml # converge staging first WHAT HAPPENED: dry run against the prod inventory; zero changes made, full delta shown. WHY IT MA TTERS: the diff artifact is what approvers review — not a prose description of intent. Nine runs out of ten die in rows 1–3. # SYMPTOM LIKELY CAUSE VERIFY FIX 1 UNREACHABLE IP wrong, host down, firewall, bastion missing ping IP → ssh user@ip by hand → -m ping - vvv Correct ansible_host , open port 22, set ProxyJump 2 Permission denied (publickey) Key not deployed, wrong key, 0600 broken on /mnt/c ssh -i key user@ip by hand ssh-copy-id , point ansible_ssh_private_key_file , keep keys in WSL home 3 Failed to escalate privilege Sudo needs password / not granted / requiretty sudo -n true on target as automation user Scoped NOP ASSWD, --ask- become-pass , drop requiretty 4 MODULE FAILURE: python: command not found No Python on minimal image raw: which python3 Bootstrap python3 via raw , set ansible_python_interpreter 5 ERROR! Syntax Error (YAML) Indent mix, tabs, CRLF from Windows editor yamllint , cat -A shows ^M 2-space indent, LF endings, lint gate in CI 6 AnsibleUndefinedVari able Typo, group_vars/ beside wrong file ansible-inventory -- graph --vars Fix name/path;

Prefer modules; changed_when / creates ; remove timestamps from templates 1 3 Fleet run crawls linear strategy, forks default 5, fact gathering everywhere Time with -- verbose , count hosts forks: 20+ , strategy: free where safe, gather_facts: false when unused, serial for rolling 1

CI secret → file → --vault- password-file staging pipeline runs first Env mismatch (works locally, fails CI) pinned versions? pin ansible , lint , collections in requirements*.yml identical local/CI install steps ▸ REAL - WORLD CONNECTION End-to-end: T erraform applies infra → outputs inventory → CI runs Ansible staging converge → --diff approved → prod rolling converge ( serial: "25%" ) → Prometheus changed -count drop and service health confirm → Grafana dashboard links back to commit SHA. Drift next week re-runs the same commit — CHANGED hosts are the drift report.

Push runs lint → molecule → staging check/diff (reviewed artifact) → staging converge → prod check/diff → approval → rolling prod converge with vault secrets from CI, verified by inventory graph and observability — same playbook, different - i path. [ NEXT ] Fleet delivery works. Next: the orchestration edge — delegation, async, blocks, and running subsets. P rodu c tion · V ol 3 2 0 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 1 3 · EDGE DELEGATION · ASYNC · BLOCKS · TAGS 8 MIN ▸ WHAT — O r c hestr a tion c ontrols delegate_to runs a task on a different host than the play target. local_action runs on the control node. async / poll runs long tasks without blocking. block / rescue / always groups tasks with recovery. tags selects subsets. RUN ELSEWHERE , RUN LONG , RUN SAFE DELEGA TE_TO act on another host ASYNC + POLL long jobs BLOCK / RESCUE recover TAGS + LIMIT subsets - name: Migrate with recovery block: - name: Run migration ansible.builtin.command: /opt/migrate.sh async: 600 poll: 10 rescue: - name: Roll back ansible.builtin.debug: msg: "migrate failed, rolling back" always: - name: Ensure app started ansible.builtin.service: name: app state: started - name: Drain from load balancer ansible.builtin.uri: url: "http://lb/drain?host={{ inventory_hostname }}" delegate_to: localhost run_once: true Run subsets: ansible-playbook site.yml --tags deploy --limit web . P rodu c tion · V ol 3 2 1 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 1 3 · EDGE ( CONT . ) DELEGATION · ASYNC · BLOCKS · TAGS 8 MIN ▸ WHY — R e a l runs need es ca pe h a t c hes Migrations fail mid-fleet; long jobs exceed SSH timeouts; load balancers must drain one host at a time; operators need to run only deploy tags at 2am. Without these controls every edge case becomes a separate playbook — with them, one playbook handles happy path, slow path, and failure path. ▸ WHERE DOES IT FIT — E dge a fter produ c tion CI/CD delivery (Ch 12) runs the standard path → this chapter handles the non-standard: different host (delegate) → long job (async) → failure (block/rescue) → subset (tags/limit) These are execution modifiers, not new declarative models. T each them last because each assumes the learner already reads plays, data flow, handlers, and rolling updates fluently. ▸ HOW IT WORKS — W here , how long , wh a t if , whi c h Delegation: task executes on delegate_to host but inventory_hostname still refers to original target — use for LB/API calls about the target. run_once: true + delegate_to: localhost runs a single API call, not once per host. Async: async: 600 (max seconds) + poll: 10 (check interval); poll: 0 fires and continues (collect

▶ CHAPTER 1 3 · EDGE ( CONT . ) DELEGATION · ASYNC · BLOCKS · TAGS 8 MIN ▸ PRACTICAL — P rove res c ue + a syn c COMMAND ──────────────────────── ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini rescue-demo.yml --tags migrate Expected: failing block task → rescue debug runs → always service start runs → play recap failed=0 (recovered) with rescue visible. R emove rescue → recap failed=1 — proves recovery changed the outcome. Why it matters: rescue converts fleet-stopping failures into logged recoveries with service guarantees. Common failure: delegate_to without run_once on LB drain → N duplicate drains → add run_once: true . ▸ WHAT CAN FAIL SYMPTOM LIKELY CAUSE PREVENTION LB drained N times delegate_to runs per host run_once: true for singleton API calls Async job lost poll: 0 without async_status follow-up until/retries/delay poller task with ansible_job_id rescue masks real failure Over-broad rescue hides root cause Rescue logs + re-raises ( fail: ) when unrecoverable; alert, not silence --tags runs nothing Tag typo or never tag not requested --list-tags before run; audit tag names in review command always CHANGED in block Imperative task without guard changed_when , creates / removes , or fai

▶ CHAPTER 1 3 · EDGE ( CONT . ) DELEGATION · ASYNC · BLOCKS · TAGS 8 MIN ▸ LAB — Ob serve / E xe c ute / V erify Objective: drain → deploy → verify → recover. Prereqs: rescue-demo.yml with block/rescue/always + drain task. 1. Run with --list-tags → Observe available subsets 2. Run --tags migrate with failing migration → V erify rescue + always both ran, recap recovered 3. Convert long task to async: 300 / poll: 0 + async_status poller → V erify non-blocking completion 4. Add delegate_to: localhost / run_once: true to drain → V erify single drain for whole batch. Failure drill: remove run_once → observe duplicate drains → restore; remove rescue → observe hard failure → restore. ▸ I nterview c he c k Interview When do y ou delegat e, async, block , or tag? Delegate when the action concerns another host (LB, API, control node). Async when the job outlasts comfortable SSH blocking. Block/rescue/always when failure needs scoped recovery with guaranteed cleanup. T ags + limit when the operator must run a named subset safely. ▶ CHAPTER 0 1 · FOUNDATIONS WHY AUTOMATION BEATS SCRIPTS 5 MIN   ي ب ر ع ح ر ش ؟ A utom a tion ا ذ ا م ل ا في ً ستخدم أساس ُ ( ت Open-Sour ce مفتوحة المصدر ) Automation « أداة Ansible » )تجهيز البنية Infrastr ucture Provisioning ة الإعدادات( و )إدار Configuration Management « يصل إليها Ansible »و ، YAML )الحالة المطلوبة( في ملف Desired State ة: تصف التحتية(. الفكر « يقارن المطلوب بالواقع ثم يقرر: Ansible ا«، بينما » ً ذ الأمر مجدد ّ العادي يقول »نف Script بنفسه. « — تسليم Ansible ة مسؤولية » ، والإعداد داخل الأجهز Terrafor m بنى بـ ُ . البنية التحتية ت ok أم changed دواج فيه. واضح لا از Automation · Desired State · YAML · Terrafor m · changed / ok ▸ WHAT — T he a utom a tion pro b lem Manual operation scales linearly with machines and fails quietly. Shell scripts capture *commands* but not *intent*: which machines, what state, what if state already exists, how to verify, how to retry. Configuration drifts. Knowledge lives in runbooks and heads. MANUAL LOOP VS DECLARATIVE CONVERGE MANUAL Operator → SSH for-loop → hosts one by one → drift accumulates → re-run repeats side effects DECLARATIVE Playbook → control node → inventory select → compare desired vs current → CHANGED or OK, au

▶ CHAPTER 0 1 · FOUNDATIONS ( CONT . ) WHY AUTOMATION BEATS SCRIPTS 5 MIN ▸ WHERE DOES IT FIT — Ec osystem l a ne Script (Bash): "run this command again" → no convergence check Image baking (P acker): snapshot state → not day-2 config Provisioner (T erraform): creates infrastructure → hands off to Ansible for inside-OS config Orchestrator (K8s): schedules containers → Ansible can provision/configure K8s nodes themselves Decision tree (preview, detailed in PDF3): WHAT ARE YOU AUTOMATING? → Infrastructure → Terraform/OpenTofu → Host/app config → Ansible Same question, three answers — the comparison that decides the tool: QUESTION SHELL LOOP ANSIBLE Which machines? Hosts hardcoded in the loop Inventory selects by group and pattern Already correct? Runs again blindly Reports OK , changes nothing Proof it worked? Exit code of the last host Per-host recap, every host Repeat next week? Hope nothing changed Converge again with the same file F ound a tions · V ol 1 4 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 1 · FOUNDATIONS ( CONT . ) WHY AUTOMATION BEATS SCRIPTS 5 MIN ▸ TERRAFORM VS ANSIBLE — P rovision vs c onfigure Terraform provisions infrastructure (creates it: VPCs, VMs, DNS, load balancers) and tracks it in a state file. Ansible configur es what already exists (OS, packages, files, services, users) and converges it on every run, keeping no state of its own. ASPECT TERRAFORM / OPENTOFU ANSIBLE Owns Infrastructure lifecycle (create, change, destroy) Inside-OS desired state (configure, converge) State State file ( terraform.tfstate ) maps config to real resources Stateless; compares desired vs current on the host each run Runs plan previews infra diff; apply changes infra --check --diff previews config diff; run converges hosts Re-run cost Re-plans against APIs; safe but slow Re-converges; OK where already correct, fast Secrets Provider creds + sensitive outputs Vault-encrypted vars, no_log , become scoping Combined workflow (the normal production shape): Terraform apply → outputs IPs/hostnames → generated inventory → Ansible configures OS/apps → services verified terraform output -json > tf-out.json # ips of new VMs ansible-playbook -i inventories/prod site.yml Handoff

▶ CHAPTER 0 1 · FOUNDATIONS ( CONT . ) WHY AUTOMATION BEATS SCRIPTS 5 MIN ▸ HOW IT WORKS — H igh - level loop USER → ansible-playbook → CONTROL NODE (inventory, vars, tasks) → SSH/WinRM → MANAGED NODE (module) → TARGET STATE → RESULT (OK/CHANGED/FAILED) ▸ PRACTICAL — N ot yet exe c ut ab le ( intention a l ) This chapter builds motivation. Execution begins in Ch 02–03. No commands to mis-run yet. ▸ WHAT CAN FAIL — M isunderst a nding a utom a tion SYMPTOM LIKELY CAUSE PREVENTION Automation reintroduces drift Scripts without idempotency Teach CHANGED vs OK early (Ch 05) Over-automation of infra as config Using Ansible to create VPCs Handoff callout: provision vs configure ▸ REAL - WORLD CONNECTION SRE uses Ansible to converge fleet after patch window: same playbook against staging then production, diff mode first, check mode for approval. ▸ I nterview c he c k Interview Why not just r un shell scr ipts via SSH loop? Scripts describe commands; automation must describe targets, desired state, convergence check, error handling, and audit result. Ansible's model adds selection, declaration, and verification around the transport that a loop lacks. [ NEXT ] We know *why* to automate. Next

▶ CHAPTER 0 2 · ARCHITECTURE AGENTLESS — CONTROL TO MANAGED 6 MIN   A r c hite c ture : ي ب ر ع ح ر ش و (« Ansible ت عليه » ّ مثب Linux Server )جهازك أو Control Node نين: ّ من مكو Architecture و Linux في SSH (. الاتصال عبر Ubuntu / CentOS المستهدفة مثل Servers ) Managed Nodes Servers ، والمتطلب الوحيد على Public/Pr ivate Key Pair بمفتاحي Windows في WinRM/SSH ، ثم JSON ، يعيد Module ذ ّ « يتصل، ينف Ansible » — ف َ على المستهد Agents . لا Python هو بيئة Linux . Control Node كـ WSL استخدم بيئة Windows يغادر. على Control Node · Managed Nodes · SSH · WinRM · Python · Agentless ▸ WHAT — A gentless a r c hite c ture Ansible requires no permanently running agent on managed nodes. The control node holds automation content and initiates connections; managed nodes receive module payloads and execute them. AGENTLESS EXECUTION PATH CONTROL NODE playbook · inv entory · vars → SSH / WinRM connection plugin → MANAGED NODE module runs · JSON b ack Linux OpenSSH + Py thon 3 Windows WinRM + P owerShell ┌───────────────────┐ │ CONTROL NODE │ │ ansible-playbook │ │ inventory │ │ variables │ │ modules (FQCN) │ └─────────┬─────────┘ │ SSH / WinRM (connection plugins) ┌───────┴────────┐ ↓ ↓ HOST 01 (Lin

▶ CHAPTER 0 2 · ARCHITECTURE ( CONT . ) AGENTLESS — CONTROL TO MANAGED 6 MIN ▸ WHERE DOES IT FIT — E xe c ution model COMMAND → LOAD CONFIG (ansible.cfg) → LOAD INVENTORY → SELECT HOSTS → LOAD VARIABLES/FACTS → PROCESS PLAY → EXECUTE TASK → RUN MODULE → RETURN RESULT → NEXT TASK This lane is the visual anchor reused every chapter. ▸ HOW IT WORKS Control node: where ansible / ansible-playbook runs. Needs Python 3.11+, collections, inventory, ansible.cfg . Managed node: target host. Needs Python (most modules) or P owerShell (Windows), SSH/WinRM reachable, privilege path ( become ). Transpor t: connection plugin. Default ssh (Linux), winrm / psrp (Windows). Data sent: module payload + args; result returned as JSON. Module ex ecution: module runs on managed node (or locally if delegate_to: localhost ), reports changed , failed , skipped . Config loading order (callout): ansible.cfg precedence: ANSIBLE_CONFIG env → ./ansible.cfg → ~/.ansible.cfg → /etc/ansible/ansible.cfg ▸ PRACTICAL — V erify c ontrol node $ ansible --version ansible [core 2.16.x] ... Meaning: confirms control node install. T arget: local. Internal: loads config, no inventory needed. Expected: version + config path. F

▶ CHAPTER 0 2 · ARCHITECTURE ( CONT . ) AGENTLESS — CONTROL TO MANAGED 6 MIN ▸ WSL SETUP — C ontrol node on W indows Windows cannot run Ansible natively. WSL2 + Ubuntu is the supported control node: a real Linux kernel where ansible- playbook , Python, and OpenSSH behave exactly like CI. wsl --install -d Ubuntu # Windows Terminal (admin): installs WSL2 + Ubuntu sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3 python3-pip pipx openssh-client git pipx install ansible # ansible + ansible-playbook on PATH pipx inject ansible ansible-lint ansible --version # expect: ansible [core 2.16.x], python 3.11+ Rules that prevent an entire class of failures: Keep the project inside WSL home ( ~/ansible/ ), not /mnt/c/ — Windows mounts are slow and cannot hold Linux permissions (SSH keys at 0600 silently break there) Use VS Code with the WSL Remote extension so editors save with LF endings; CRLF line endings corrupt Y AML and vault files Generate the SSH key inside WSL ( ssh-keygen -t ed25519 ), copy the public half to servers with ssh-copy-id One .venv or pipx per toolset; never sudo pip install (breaks system Python) ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "ansible-control" # ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 ssh-copy-id ansibl

No agent deployed to 200 hosts; rotation handled by SSH key management. ▸ I nterview c he c k Interview Why is Ansible called agentless? Managed nodes need no permanent Ansible daemon. Control node connects via SSH/WinRM per task and executes modules on demand. [ NEXT ] Architecture tells *how* Ansible reaches machines. Next: *which* machines — inventory and targeting. ▶ CHAPTER 0 3 · INVENTORY INVENTORY — WHICH MACHINES 7 MIN   ـ ل ا I nventory ي ب ر ع ح ر ش : ل ا ص ت ا ل ا و مثل Groups مقسمة إلى Managed Nodes الـ IPs ( يسر د عناو ين hosts.ini )مثل Inventory ملف ز الدخول بلا ّ ث الداخل إعداداتها. جه فير children ا لمجموعات عبر � ، والمجموعة قد تكون أم [db] و [web] (، انسخ Control Node ا على � يبقى سر Private Key )الخاص ssh-keygen بأمر Key Pair د ّ كلمة سر: ول ومفتاح ansible_user و ansible_host ات الوصول مثل ة. متغير مباشر ssh ب ّ ، ثم جر ssh-copy-id العام بـ . ProxyJump « كيف يصل، وخلف بوابة اقفز عبر Ansible تشر ح لـ» ansible_ssh_pr ivate_key_file Inventory · Groups · hosts.ini · ssh-keygen · ssh-copy-id · ansible_host ▸ WHAT — I nventory is t a rget de c l a r a tion Inventory lists managed nodes and organizes them into groups . Playbooks select from this list; ad hoc commands address it directly. INVENTORY HIERARCHY INVENT ORY FILE → GROUPS web · db · pr od → HOSTS web-01 · db-01 → VARS group_vars · host_v ars Static inventory example: [web] web-01 ansible_host=10.0.1.11 web-02 ansible_host=10.0.1.12 [db] db-01 ansible_host=10.0.1.21 [prod:children] web db Hierarchy: INVENTORY +-- groups (web, db, prod) +-- hosts (web-01, web-02) +-- group_v

▶ CHAPTER 0 3 · INVENTORY ( CONT . ) INVENTORY — WHICH MACHINES 7 MIN ▸ HOW IT WORKS Static: INI or Y AML file, committed to repo, versioned. Dynamic: plugin queries cloud (A WS EC2, Azure) at runtime — generates inventory, not checked in. Patterns: web , web[0] , web:db , prod:&web , all:!db — composed at CLI/play hosts: . Variables: inventory vars flow into variable precedence (taught fully in PDF2 Ch 06) via group_vars/web.yml , host_vars/db-01.yml . ▸ PRACTICAL — A d ho c proof ( first exe c ution ) Ad hoc = single task without playbook. Proves inventory + transport before Y AML complexity. COMMAND ──────────────────────── ansible web -i inventory.ini -m ping Meaning: run ping module against group web . Target: web-01 , web-02 . Internal: control node loads inventory, selects hosts, sends ping.py via SSH, returns JSON. Expected: RESULT ──────────────────────── web-01 | SUCCESS => { "changed": false, "ping": "pong" } web-02 | SUCCESS => { "changed": false, "ping": "pong" } Why it matters: proves selection, transport, Python on target in 5 seconds. Common failure: UNREACHABLE → check ansible_user , ansible_host , key, ansible -m ping with -vvv changed: false surprise → ping is ch

▶ CHAPTER 0 3 · INVENTORY ( CONT . ) INVENTORY — WHICH MACHINES 7 MIN ▸ CONNECTING — SSH keys , users , IP s Inventory names the targets; connection variables explain how to reach them . Four variables do 95% of the work: [web] web-01 ansible_host=10.0.1.11 ansible_user=ansible ansible_port=22 web-02 ansible_host=10.0.1.12 ansible_user=ansible [web:vars] ansible_ssh_private_key_file=~/.ssh/id_ed25519 ansible_become=true ansible_host — real IP/hostname (the inventory name stays a stable alias even when IPs change) ansible_user — SSH login user; create a dedicated ansible user, never automate as root over SSH ansible_port — non-default SSH port where hardened ansible_ssh_private_key_file — which key; one key per environment ( prod_ed25519 vs staging_ed25519 ) Key bootstrap (once per server, from the control node): ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/prod_ed25519 # private stays 0600, never leaves control node ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/prod_ed25519 ansible@10.0.1.11 ssh -i ~/.ssh/prod_ed25519 ansible@10.0.1.11 # must log in with no password prompt Behind a bastion, hop transparently instead of copying keys around: F ound a tions · V ol 1 1 3 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 3 · INVENTORY ( CONT . ) INVENTORY — WHICH MACHINES 7 MIN ▸ CONNECTING — Ba stions , first c ont ac t , trust [web:vars] ansible_ssh_common_args=-o ProxyJump=bastion.example.com First-contact checklist (in order, stop at the first red): ping -c2 10.0.1.11 # IP reachable at all? ssh ansible@10.0.1.11 # key auth works by hand? ansible web-01 -i inventory.ini -m ping # Ansible transport works? ansible web -i inventory.ini --list-hosts # pattern selects who you think? Host-key trust: first connection prompts Are you sure you want to continue connecting? . For known fleets, pre-seed ~/.ssh/known_hosts with ssh-keyscan ; setting host_key_checking=false in ansible.cfg silences the prompt but also silences real machine-in-the-middle warnings — scope it to ephemeral lab inventories only. ▸ WHAT CAN FAIL Pattern selects zero hosts → hosts: web matches nothing if group misspelled → --list-hosts verify Wrong vars file location → group_vars/ must sit beside inventory file Dynamic inventory creds → plugin fails silently if cloud creds missing ▸ REAL - WORLD CONNECTION Staging vs prod: same playbook, different inventories ( inventories/staging/ , inventories/prod/ ). Promotion = chang

▶ CHAPTER 0 3 · INVENTORY ( CONT . ) INVENTORY — WHICH MACHINES 7 MIN ▸ LAB — Ob serve / E xe c ute / V erify Objective: prove inventory selection. Prereqs: inventory.ini above. S teps: 1. ansible all -i inventory.ini --list-hosts → Observe all targets 2. ansible web -i inventory.ini -m ping → Execute + W atch CHANGED vs SUC CESS 3. Verify pong . Explain: ping validates transport, not config. Failure scenarios: wrong ansible_host → UNREA CHABLE; fix → correct IP. ▸ I nterview c he c k Interview Static vs dynamic inv entory? Static lists hosts in file; dynamic generates list at runtime from cloud API. S tatic for stable fleet, dynamic for elastic/autoscaling. [ NEXT ] We know *which* machines. Next: *what* state they should reach — playbooks. F ound a tions · V ol 1 1 5 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 4 · PLAYBOOKS PLAYBOOK — DESIRED STATE IN YAML 8 MIN   ل و أ P l a y b ook : ي ب ر ع ح ر ش ،( ansible all -i hosts.ini -m ping واحدة بلا ملف )مثال: Task ذ ّ ينف Ad-hoc Command الأمر السر يع Plays يحوي YAML فملف Playbook . أما ansible gr oup -i file -m module -a ar gs وصيغته العامة حساسة YAML ا. لغة ً واحد Module منها ٌّ يستدعي كل Tasks وتضم hosts تستهدف مجموعة Play ، وكل مثل FQCN م مسافتين، واستخدم أسماء كاملة ، والتز Tab ، ممنوع --- للمسافات: ابدأ بـ . --check وعاين بـ --syntax-check . قبل التشغيل افحص بـ ansible.builtin.p ackage Ad-hoc Commands · Playbook · Tasks · YAML · FQCN · --check ▸ WHAT — P l a y b ook is desired - st a te do c ument A playbook maps hosts to tasks that invoke modules with arguments . It is Y AML, declarative: describe end state, not step- by-step shell. PLAY NESTS TASKS , TASKS INVOKE MODULES PLAY hosts · become → TASK name → MODULE ansible.builtin.* → ARGS name · stat e ▸ WHY — F rom a d ho c to repe a t ab le Ad hoc proves one module once. Playbooks repeat, order, and audit multiple tasks. They are the unit committed to Git and triggered by CI. ASPECT AD HOC COMMAND PLAYBOOK Shape One module call from the CLI Plays and tasks in a Y AML file

▶ CHAPTER 0 4 · PLAYBOOKS ( CONT . ) PLAYBOOK — DESIRED STATE IN YAML 8 MIN ▸ YAML — S ynt a x b efore sem a nti c s - name: Configure web server hosts: web become: true # privilege escalation tasks: - name: Install nginx ansible.builtin.package: name: nginx state: present - name: Ensure nginx running ansible.builtin.service: name: nginx state: started enabled: true Hierarchy: PLAY (hosts: web, become: true) +-- tasks +-- TASK (name: Install nginx) +-- MODULE (ansible.builtin.package, FQCN) +-- ARGUMENTS (name, state) Rule: FQCN always ( ansible.builtin.* ) — short names obsolete. Y AML whitespace matters; 2-space indent. ▸ HOW IT WORKS — E xe c ution PLAY (web) → TASK 1 (package) → SSH → managed node → check nginx absent → install → CHANGED → TASK 2 (service) → check stopped → start → CHANGED → RESULT per host → NEXT PLAY Play = which hosts; T ask = what module with which args; Module = implementation that converges state. F ound a tions · V ol 1 1 7 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 4 · PLAYBOOKS ( CONT . ) PLAYBOOK — DESIRED STATE IN YAML 8 MIN ▸ PRACTICAL — R un it COMMAND ──────────────────────── ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini site.yml Meaning: execute playbook against inventory. T arget: web group. Internal: load site.yml , select hosts, for each task send module, collect changed/ok/failed . Expected: RESULT ──────────────────────── PLAY [Configure web server] *** TASK [Install nginx] *** changed: [web-01] TASK [Ensure nginx running] *** changed: [web-01] PLAY RECAP *** web-01 : ok=2 changed=2 failed=0 Why it matters: proves declarative convergence; re-run should yield ok=2 changed=0 . Common failure: Y AML parse error → ERROR! Syntax Error at line; fix indent or missing : . ▸ WHAT CAN FAIL hosts: web matches zero → skipping: no hosts matched → verify with --list-hosts become: true without sudo → Failed to escalate → ansible_become_user / sudoers Module args typo → unsupported parameter → check ansible-doc ansible.builtin.package F ound a tions · V ol 1 1 8 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 4 · PLAYBOOKS ( CONT . ) PLAYBOOK — DESIRED STATE IN YAML 8 MIN ▸ REAL - WORLD CONNECTION Team commits site.yml to infra/ repo; reviewer sees state: present intent, not apt-get install imperative. ▸ LAB — Ob serve / E xe c ute / V erify Observe: nginx absent ( systemctl status nginx fails). Execute: ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini site.yml -- check --diff (dry run). V erify: --diff shows planned changes. Execute for real, verify ok with changed=2 , re-run verify changed=0 . ▸ I nterview c he c k Interview Play vs task vs module? Play selects hosts and holds tasks; task invokes one module with arguments; module does work on managed node and reports convergence. [ NEXT ] Playbooks declare state. Next: how modules enforce idempotency and report CHANGED vs OK. F ound a tions · V ol 1 1 9 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 5 · IDEMPOTENCY MODULES AND IDEMPOTENCY ADV   ـ ل ا M odules و I dempoten c y : ي ب ر ع ح ر ش ر سلوك ّ يغي Plugin (، بينما Service مة، نسخ ملف، إدارة ة )تثبيت حز وحدة عمل جاهز Module الـ ر ّ لا يغي Script ار نفس : تكر Idempot ency شيح(. الخاصية الجوهر ية « نفسه )اتصال، بحث، تر Ansible » ( لا إعادة تثبيت، وتغيير فعلي Desired S tate في Server )أخضر: ok ا يعني ً ا بلا حاجة — مثبت مسبق ً شيئ لتحصل command/shell على Modules ل ّ )أحمر(. فض failed )أصفر(، وخطأ يعني changed يعني ا. ً تلقائي check mode ودعم Idempotency على Modules · Plugins · Idempot ency · ok · changed · failed ▸ WHAT — M odule + ide a l result Module = unit of desired state. T akes args, checks current state, acts only if needed, returns JSON with changed , failed , msg . FIRST RUN — CHANGED Desired: nginx present ↓ Current: absent ↓ Install → CHANGED SECOND RUN — OK Desired: nginx present ↓ Current: present ↓ No action → OK Idempotency: same input applied twice → same end state, second run reports no change. ▸ WHY — D esired st a te ≠ re - run c omm a nds Scripts re-run commands blindly. Modules compare desired vs current: DESIRED STATE (state: present) ↓ CURRENT STATE (nginx absent? present?) ↓ COMPARE → C

▶ CHAPTER 0 5 · IDEMPOTENCY ( CONT . ) MODULES AND IDEMPOTENCY ADV ▸ HOW IT WORKS — V isu a l First run: Desired: nginx present → Current: absent → Install → CHANGED Second run: Desired: nginx present → Current: present → No action → OK Result states (always labeled with symbol+color, not color alone): OK (green ●) — converged, no change CHANGED (blue ◐ ) — converged, did change FAILED (red ��) — did not converge SKIPPED (gray ○) — conditional skipped UNREACHABLE (amber ��) — transport failed DESIRED VS CURRENT DECIDES EVERYTHING DESIRED → CURRENT → COMPARE → CHANGE or NO-OP F ound a tions · V ol 1 2 1 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 5 · IDEMPOTENCY ( CONT . ) MODULES AND IDEMPOTENCY ADV ▸ PRACTICAL — Ob serve idempoten c y - name: Idempotency demo hosts: web tasks: - name: Create app directory ansible.builtin.file: path: /opt/app state: directory mode: '0755' First run: changed: [web-01] . Second run: ok: [web-01] . Proof of desired-state model. Check and diff modes: $ ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini site.yml --check --diff --check dry-runs, --diff shows planned file/service changes. Use for approval gates. ▸ WHAT CAN FAIL — C ommon misre a ds OK misread as "nothing happened" → actually "already converged" (GO TCHA callout below) Module not idempotent by misuse → command: apt-get install always CHANGED vs package: converges → use package / file / template not command / shell where module exists changed_when abuse → masks real change signal [ GOTCHA ] "OK" does not mean Ansible did nothing meaningful. It means desired state already holds. Always read result state pair: ok vs changed count. F ound a tions · V ol 1 2 2 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 5 · IDEMPOTENCY ( CONT . ) MODULES AND IDEMPOTENCY ADV ▸ COMMAND + RESULT PATTERN COMMAND ──────────────────────── ansible web -i inventory.ini -m ansible.builtin.file -a "path=/opt/app state=directory mode=0755" RESULT ──────────────────────── web-01 | CHANGED => { "changed": true, "path": "/opt/app", "state": "directory" } WHAT HAPPENED: file module ensured directory exists, created it. WHY IT MATTERS: proves CHANGED on creation, OK on repeat. COMMON FAILURE: path parent missing → use state=directory (creates parents), mode typo → permission drift. ▸ COMPARISON — M odule vs shell ASPECT MODULE ( F I L E , P A C K A G E ) C O M M A N D / S H E L L Intent desired state imperative command Idempotency built-in compare always CHANGED unless creates / removes Check mode supported skipped Audit diff friendly opaque ▸ REAL - WORLD CONNECTION Patch fleet: re-run same playbook weekly → CHANGED only where drift occurred. changed count becomes drift metric fed to observability. ▸ I nterview c he c k Interview What mak es a module idempot ent? It compares desired vs current state and acts only when different, reporting CHANGED when it acted and OK when already converged. [ NEXT ]

▶ APPENDIX · CHEATSHEET CHEATSHEET — FQCN AND FAILURES FINALE A FQCN — U se A lw a ys LEGACY FQCN yum , apt ansible.builtin.package template ansible.builtin.template service ansible.builtin.service file ansible.builtin.file B Fa ilure I ndex SYMPTOM FIX UNREA CHABLE SSH key / ansible_host Failed to escalate become + sudoers YAML error ansible-lint OK misread already converged ● OK — c onverged , no c h a nge ◐ CHANGED — c onverged , did c h a nge �� FAILED — did not c onverge F ound a tions · V ol 1 2 4 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 6 · DATA FLOW VARIABLES · FACTS · REGISTERS 8 MIN   Va ri ab les ي ب ر ع ح ر ش : Fac ts و Play ، متغيرات group_vars/host_v ars تكتبها أنت )ملفات Variables القيم تأتي من ثلاثة منابع: ، setup ين، الذاكر ة( عبر )نظام التشغيل، العناو Server ا عن كل ً « تلقائي Ansible يجمعها » Facts و ،( Task و ّ : الأخص Precedence ض نفس الاسم تحسم لاحقة. عند تعار Tasks سابقة ل Task تحفظ ناتج Registers و debug ا بأمر ً تغلب الجميع بلا استثناء. تحقق دائم Extra V ars (-e) ات سطر الأوامر ، ومتغير ّ يغلب الأعم . Templat es قبل Variables · Facts · Registers · Precedence · Extra V ars (-e) · debug ▸ WHAT — T hree sour c es of d a t a Variables parameterize desired state. F acts are auto-gathered system data. R egisters capture task output for later use. DATA FLOWS DOWNHILL TO MODULES Inventory → group/host v ars → play/task v ars → facts + r egisters → module / t emplat e Variables: author-defined values ( app_port: 8080 ) from inventory, group_vars/ , host_vars/ , play, task, or --extra- vars . Facts: discovered values ( ansible_os_family , ansible_default_ipv4.address ) collected by ansible.builtin.setup at play start (gather_facts). Registers: per-host results of a prior task ( register: host

▶ CHAPTER 0 6 · DATA FLOW ( CONT . ) VARIABLES · FACTS · REGISTERS 8 MIN ▸ HOW IT WORKS — P re c eden c e , f ac ts , registers Precedence exists because specificity must win: general defaults lose to host-specific values. Simplified order (low → high): role defaults → group_vars/all → group_vars/web → host_vars/web-01 → play vars → task vars → extra- vars Collision example: group_vars/all.yml sets app_port: 8080 , host_vars/web-01.yml sets app_port: 9090 → web-01 renders 9090, others render 8080. ansible-playbook -e app_port=9999 overrides everything (operator intent wins for one run). Facts: gather_facts: true (default) runs setup first, populating ansible_facts . Disable with gather_facts: false for speed when facts are unused. R egisters: register stores stdout , stderr , rc , changed per host — never shared across hosts unless hostvars is read explicitly. ASPECT VARIABLE FACT REGISTER Author You write it Ansible discovers it A task captures it Example app_port: 8080 ansible_facts.os_family host_out.stdout Refresh File-defined rank Re-gathered every run Re-registered every run Override --extra-vars wins Cannot override, only use Read via hostvars cross-host E ngineering · V ol

▶ CHAPTER 0 6 · DATA FLOW ( CONT . ) VARIABLES · FACTS · REGISTERS 8 MIN ▸ PRACTICAL — Ob serve d a t a flow - name: Show data flow hosts: web vars: app_port: 8080 tasks: - name: Show variable ansible.builtin.debug: msg: "port {{ app_port }}" - name: Capture hostname ansible.builtin.command: cat /etc/hostname register: host_out changed_when: false - name: Show captured output ansible.builtin.debug: var: host_out.stdout - name: Show discovered fact ansible.builtin.debug: msg: "family {{ ansible_facts.os_family }}" COMMAND ──────────────────────── ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini data.yml -e app_port=9999 Meaning: run play with CLI override. Expected: msg: "port 9999" on all hosts — proves extra-vars beats file vars. R emove - e → web-01 shows 9090 (host_vars), others 8080. Why it matters: proves precedence is deterministic, not magic. Common failure: quoting msg="port {{ app_port }}" with double quotes inside Y AML double quotes → use single outer or block scalar. E ngineering · V ol 2 5 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 6 · DATA FLOW ( CONT . ) VARIABLES · FACTS · REGISTERS 8 MIN ▸ WHAT CAN FAIL SYMPTOM LIKELY CAUSE PREVENTION AnsibleUndefinedVariable: 'app_port' is undefined Typo or vars file in wrong directory group_vars/ must sit beside inventory file; verify with ansible-inventory --graph --vars Precedence surprise (wrong port) Higher-specificity file wins silently debug: var=app_port per host before template task host_out.stdout empty Task skipped/failed before register Check host_out.rc , host_out.skipped ; guard with when: host_out.rc is defined Facts missing gather_facts: false set globally Re-enable per play or call ansible.builtin.setup explicitly [ GOTCHA ] Precedence is not inheritance depth — it is specificity + source rank. Group of one host still loses to that host's host_vars. Always verify with --list-hosts + debug before templating. ▸ REAL - WORLD CONNECTION Team stores defaults in group_vars/all.yml (port, TLS paths), per-environment overrides in group_vars/prod.yml , per- host exceptions in host_vars/ . Promotion from staging to prod changes inventory path, not playbook. changed counts stay clean because data varies, not tasks. E ngineering · V ol 2 6 ok c h a nged

▶ CHAPTER 0 6 · DATA FLOW ( CONT . ) VARIABLES · FACTS · REGISTERS 8 MIN ▸ LAB — Ob serve / E xe c ute / V erify Objective: prove precedence + facts + registers. Prereqs: group_vars/all.yml ( app_port: 8080 ), host_vars/web- 01.yml ( app_port: 9090 ). 1. ansible-inventory -i inventory.ini --graph --vars → Observe merged vars per host 2. ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini data.yml --check → Execute dry run, watch msg per host 3. Verify web-01 shows 9090, others 8080. Explain: host specificity wins. 4. Re-run with -e app_port=9999 → Verify all show 9999. Explain: operator override is highest rank. Failure drill: rename host_vars/ to hostvars/ → re-run → undefined/wrong value → fix directory name. ▸ I nterview c he c k Interview Where do variables come fr om, and which wins? Inventory, group/host vars files, play/task vars, facts, registers, extra-vars. More specific beats more general; extra-vars beats files. Facts are discovered, registers are captured per host from prior task results. [ NEXT ] Data varies per host. Next: branch and repeat with that data — conditionals, loops, filters. E ngineering · V ol 2 7 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 7 · LOGIC CONDITIONALS · LOOPS · FILTERS 7 MIN   C ondition a ls ي ب ر ع ح ر ش : L oops و ر نفس ال ّ أو نتيجة سابقة( وكر Variable أو Fact )يعمل فقط إذا تحقق شر ط من when ه التنفيذ بشرط ّ وج ل القيم ّ ر القائمة وتجاوز ما لا يطابق الشر ط. حو ّ ا: كر ً بدل نسخها، واجمعهما مع loop على قائمة بـ Task . انتبه: شرط join/length و ternary للقيم الغائبة و default مثل Filters شحات بمر Templat es داخل . until/retries/delay دار بـ ُ الانتظار الطو يل ت Tasks ، و {{ }} ا بلا أقواس ً كتب عاري ُ ي when when · loop · Filters · default · until · {{ }} ▸ WHAT — B r a n c h , repe a t , tr a nsform Conditionals ( when ) branch tasks. Loops ( loop ) repeat one task over many items. Filters transform data inside Jinja2 expressions ( {{ value | filter }} ). - name: Install nginx only on web ansible.builtin.package: name: nginx state: present when: inventory_hostname in groups['web'] - name: Ensure users exist ansible.builtin.user: name: "{{ item }}" state: present loop: [alice, bob] Jinja2 filters: {{ app_port | default(8080) }} , {{ groups['web'] | length }} , {{ app_name | upper }} . ▸ WHY — F leets diverge Real fleets are not uniform: web needs nginx, db needs postgres; ten users, not one.

▶ CHAPTER 0 7 · LOGIC ( CONT . ) CONDITIONALS · LOOPS · FILTERS 7 MIN ▸ HOW IT WORKS — E v a lu a tion per host when is a Jinja2 expression evaluated per host, without {{ }} delimiters. loop executes the task once per item, with item and ansible_loop metadata. Filters pipe left value through right function; they chain ( {{ name | lower | trim }} ). Combined example: - name: Deploy app config per host ansible.builtin.template: src: app.conf.j2 dest: /etc/app/app.conf loop: "{{ app_instances }}" when: app_enabled | default(true) Loop over app_instances (from group vars), skipped entirely when app_enabled is false. loop_control: label keeps output readable for long lists. BRANCH PER HOST AT RUN TIME WHEN TRUE Task runs on this host → module converges → result recorded WHEN FALSE Task SKIPPED on this host → play continues → no change, no failure E ngineering · V ol 2 9 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 7 · LOGIC ( CONT . ) CONDITIONALS · LOOPS · FILTERS 7 MIN ▸ FILTER FIELD GUIDE — T he dozen th a t ca rry you Filters group by job. Learn these twelve and you can read any playbook: JOB FILTERS EXAMPLE Missing-safe default , is defined {{ app_port | default(8080) }} Branch in one line ternary {{ tls_enabled | ternary('https', 'http') }} Types int , bool , string , list {{ replicas | int + 1 }} Lists length , join , map , select , unique , sort {{ groups['web'] | length }} , {{ users | map(attribute='name') | join(',') }} Dicts dict2items , combine {% for kv in app_env | dict2items %} with kv.key / kv.value Text upper , lower , trim , replace {{ app_name | lower | trim }} Data formats to_json , from_yaml , to_nice_yaml {{ cfg | to_nice_yaml }} for debug output The safety pattern first: when: myvar is defined and myvar == "x" never explodes on missing hosts; {{ myvar | default('x') }} never aborts a template. Write every optional value one of these two ways. E ngineering · V ol 2 1 0 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 7 · LOGIC ( CONT . ) CONDITIONALS · LOOPS · FILTERS 7 MIN ▸ LOOP VARIANTS — B eyond fl a t lists Dictionaries need dict2items (a dict cannot loop directly): - name: Export environment entries ansible.builtin.lineinfile: path: /etc/app/env line: "{{ item.key }}={{ item.value }}" loop: "{{ app_env | dict2items }}" Long or slow loops stay readable and controllable: - name: Pull service images ansible.builtin.command: docker pull {{ item }} loop: "{{ images }}" loop_control: label: "{{ item }}" pause: 2 Polling waits for reality instead of sleeping blindly: - name: Wait for healthy endpoint ansible.builtin.uri: url: "http://{{ inventory_hostname }}:8080/health" register: health until: health.status == 200 retries: 30 delay: 10 until re-runs the task until the condition holds (or retries run out); combine with changed_when: false for pure checks so successful polls report OK , not CHANGED . E ngineering · V ol 2 1 1 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

▶ CHAPTER 0 7 · LOGIC ( CONT . ) CONDITIONALS · LOOPS · FILTERS 7 MIN ▸ PRACTICAL — R un b r a n c h + repe a t COMMAND ──────────────────────── ansible web -i inventory.ini -m ansible.builtin.debug -a "msg={{ ansible_facts.os_family }}" Meaning: show discovered family per host. Expected: Debian / RedHat per target — proves facts exist before when uses them. - name: Guarded install hosts: all tasks: - name: Install nginx on Debian web only ansible.builtin.package: name: nginx state: present when: - inventory_hostname in groups['web'] - ansible_facts.os_family == "Debian" Why it matters: two-condition guard prevents installing on wrong OS family. Common failure: when: "{{ condition }}" with delimiters → always truthy string; write bare when: condition . E ngineering · V ol 2 1 2 ok c h a nged f a iled = 0 TOC

Handlers run once at end of play — only if notified by a task that reported CHANGED . RENDER , COMPARE , NOTIFY ONCE TEMPL ATE → COMPARE → CHANGED → notif y → HANDLER ONCE Five notifying tasks still restart the service exactly once, at play end. - name: Render nginx config ansible.builtin.template: src: nginx.conf.j2 dest: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf mode: '0644' notify: Restart nginx handlers: - name: Restart nginx ansible.builtin.service: name: nginx state: restarted Template ( nginx.conf.j2 ): server

At play end (or meta: flush_handlers mid- play), each queued handler runs once in handler order, not notify order. listen: groups multiple notify names onto one handler. handlers: - name: Restart web stack listen: Restart nginx ansible.builtin.service: name: nginx state: restarted validate: guards syntax before install ( validate: "nginx -t -c %s" ); failed validation → task FAILED , dest untouched. Conditionals Roles · Collections · Ansible Galaxy · requirements.yml · import_role · include_r ole ▸ WHAT — R eus ab le units a nd their distri b ution Role = reusable unit with conventional directories (tasks, handlers, templates, defaults, vars). Collection = versioned distribution of roles plus modules and plugins, addressed by fully qualified names ( namespace.collection ). roles/web/ tasks/main.yml handlers/main.yml templates/nginx.conf.j2 defaults/main.yml vars/main.yml meta/main.yml Conventional layout: tunables in defaults (lose), assertions in vars (win). roles/web/ tasks/main.yml handlers/main.yml templates/nginx.conf.j2 defaults/main.yml vars/main

T ask inside role resolves templates/ and files/ relative to the role. import_role is static (parsed when playbook loads — when applies per task inside). include_role is dynamic (evaluated at execution — can loop over roles). - name: Static web role ansible.builtin.import_role: name: web - name: Dynamic per-env roles ansible.builtin.include_role: name: "{{ item }}" loop: [base, web] Collections: ansible-galaxy collection install -r requirements.yml ; reference namespace.collection.module .
